history: What marking must be affixed to a high-risk AI system to indicate conformity with the regulation?
Article 16(h) requires providers to affix the CE marking to the high-risk AI system to indicate conformity with the Regulation.
followup: And what identifying information has to be on it or its packaging?
gold_standalone: What information must be provided on a high-risk AI system, its packaging or accompanying documentation to identify the provider?

history: What are high-risk AI systems intended to be used for in educational and vocational training institutions?
Annex III point 3(b) covers AI systems intended to evaluate learning outcomes, including when used to steer the learning process.
followup: What about admission or access to those institutions?
gold_standalone: What are AI systems intended to be used for in relation to access or admission to educational and vocational training institutions?

history: What are the notification requirements for using a 'real-time' remote biometric identification system in publicly accessible spaces?
Article 5(4) requires each use to be notified to the relevant market surveillance authority and the national data protection authority.
followup: For what specific purposes can it be deployed at all?
gold_standalone: For what specific purposes can 'real-time' remote biometric identification systems be deployed in publicly accessible spaces?

history: What is the intended use of AI systems by law enforcement authorities that involves assessing the risk of a natural person offending?
Annex III point 6(d) covers systems used by law enforcement to assess the risk of a natural person offending or re-offending.
followup: And when they profile people during investigations?
gold_standalone: What is the intended use of AI systems by law enforcement authorities that involves profiling natural persons in the course of investigations?

history: How long are the logs of personal data processing kept in the AI regulatory sandbox?
Article 59(1)(h) provides that logs of the processing are kept for the duration of participation in the sandbox.
followup: Does that processing affect data subjects' rights?
gold_standalone: Does the processing of personal data in the AI regulatory sandbox affect the rights of data subjects under Union law?

history: What will the Commission evaluate regarding the AI Office by 2 August 2028?
Article 112(5) asks the Commission to evaluate the functioning of the AI Office and whether it should be upgraded.
followup: And what aspect of AI development must it review by the same date?
gold_standalone: What aspect of AI development is the Commission required to review and report on by 2 August 2028?

history: What is the sole purpose of AI systems used for biometric verification that are not included in remote biometric identification?
Annex III point 1(a) excludes systems whose sole purpose is to confirm that a specific natural person is who they claim to be.
followup: What is the definition of a biometric categorisation system then?
gold_standalone: What is the purpose of a biometric categorisation system in terms of assigning natural persons to categories?

history: What must deployers do if they envisage using a high-risk AI system that has not been registered in the EU database?
Article 26(8) requires deployers to register themselves or the system in the EU database, or not to use it.
followup: If they already meet those duties through other obligations, what can go into the fundamental rights impact assessment?
gold_standalone: What can the deployer include in the fundamental rights impact assessment if the obligations are already met through other obligations?

history: When must the report be made after establishing a causal link between the AI system and a serious incident?
Article 73(2) sets the deadline for reporting a serious incident once the causal link is established.
followup: How quickly must the market surveillance authority act after receiving it?
gold_standalone: Within what time frame must the market surveillance authority take appropriate measures after receiving a serious incident report?

history: Who can submit applications for participation in AI regulatory sandboxes?
Article 58(2)(b) sets who may apply to participate in an AI regulatory sandbox.
followup: Who is liable if something goes wrong during real-world testing?
gold_standalone: Who is liable for any damage caused during testing of AI systems in real world conditions?

history: What are the obligations of providers of general-purpose AI models with systemic risk regarding model evaluation?
Article 55(1)(a) requires providers of general-purpose AI models with systemic risk to perform model evaluation with standardised protocols and tools.
followup: What characteristics make a model general-purpose in the first place?
gold_standalone: What characteristics must a general-purpose AI model display to be considered capable of performing a wide range of distinct tasks?

history: What action should market surveillance authorities take if they have sufficient reason to consider a general-purpose AI system non-compliant?
Article 75(2) directs market surveillance authorities to cooperate with the AI Office in that case.
followup: What must the AI Office do before prohibiting one on a national market?
gold_standalone: What must the AI Office do before deciding to prohibit or restrict an AI system on a national market?

history: What must the AI Office inform the provider of when conducting an inspection?
Article 75a(4) sets what the AI Office must inform the provider of when it conducts an inspection.
followup: Who can the AI Office or the competent authorities address about compliance with this Regulation?
gold_standalone: Who can be addressed by the AI Office or the competent authorities on issues related to ensuring compliance with this Regulation?

history: What authority does the Commission have to amend Annexes VI and VII in the conformity assessment process?
Article 43(5) empowers the Commission to adopt delegated acts amending Annexes VI and VII.
followup: Can it also change the classification rules for high-risk AI systems?
gold_standalone: What authority does the Commission have to amend the classification rules for high-risk AI systems?

history: What tasks does the Board have in facilitating a shared understanding among market operators and competent authorities?
Article 66(g) tasks the Board with facilitating a shared understanding of the Regulation among operators and authorities.
followup: In which fields should it prioritise cooperation with Union institutions and expert groups?
gold_standalone: In which fields should the Board prioritise cooperation with Union institutions, bodies and expert groups?

history: Under what conditions can the exit report from an AI regulatory sandbox be made publicly available?
Article 57(8) allows publication of the exit report through the single information platform under conditions.
followup: Who coordinates the sandbox activities and cooperates within the Board framework?
gold_standalone: Who are the entities responsible for coordinating AI regulatory sandbox activities and cooperating within the framework of the Board?

Article 16(h) requires providers to affix the CE marking to the high-risk AI system.

history: What is required for the use of an AI system that generates or manipulates realistic images, videos or audio of a person?
Article 5(1)(ba) addresses systems that generate or manipulate such content of identifiable persons without consent.
